title: Freeze webhook fires before ownership check
loc: src/server.js : 115 | category: authz
foundBy: ['authz-and-attribution', 'data-integrity', 'tests-that-dont-test', 'correctness'] | verifiedBy: ['refute:p1.1', 'refute:p1.2', 'refute:p1.3']
SUMMARY: The POST /accounts/:id/freeze route sends the account.freeze-requested webhook to the card processor before freezeAccount() has checked that the caller owns the account (or that it isn't already frozen), so any signed-in user can trigger that third-party notification for an account they don't own.
FAILURE: POST /accounts/:id/freeze lets any signed-in user (not just the account's owner) trigger a real account.freeze-requested webhook delivery to the external card processor for an account they don't own, naming the real owner's accountId and the attacker's own id as requestedBy -- because notify() at server.js:115 fires synchronously (unawaited) before freezeAccount() at server.js:116 performs the ownership check (404) or the already-frozen check (409) that would otherwise have blocked the request. Verified directly: a non-owner's freeze call returns 404 to the caller while the mocked webhook transport already recorded one account.freeze-requested delivery for the target account. The same ordering also double-fires the webhook when an already-frozen account is frozen again. This violates docs/security.md's 'Authorisation first' rule and departs from the save-then-notify ordering used by every other mutating route in the file.

ROOTCAUSE: In the POST /accounts/:id/freeze handler, notify('account.freeze-requested', ...) is called before freezeAccount() runs (and before store.save()), so the card processor is told to freeze an account even when the request is later rejected for lack of ownership, for being already frozen, or otherwise fails — breaking the save-then-notify pattern every other mutating route follows.

title: publicAccount never serializes frozen state
loc: src/serialize.js : 9 | category: silent-drop
foundBy: ['silent-drops', 'correctness'] | verifiedBy: ['refute:p2.1', 'refute:p2.2', 'refute:p2.3']
SUMMARY: publicAccount(), the single function every account-returning route serializes through, has no field for frozenAt (unlike closedAt, which it already exposes as `closed`), so a frozen account's API representation is byte-for-byte identical to an unfrozen one.
FAILURE: A member calls POST /accounts/:id/freeze after losing a card. The handler returns HTTP 200 with body {id, label, currency, balanceCents, closed:false, createdAt} — no frozen indicator at all, identical to the pre-freeze body (verified live: freeze response and a subsequent GET /accounts/:id and GET /accounts list are all identical to the unfrozen state, even though store.get('accounts', id) on the raw row shows frozenAt correctly set). The caller/UI that just froze the account cannot confirm the freeze took effect, a later GET cannot show the account as frozen, and the ONLY way any API consumer can discover an account is frozen is to attempt a transfer and receive the new 409 'a frozen account cannot transfer' error. The same gap applies to the admin's POST /accounts/:id/unfreeze response and to every other route that returns an account (POST /accounts, GET /accounts/:id, GET /accounts list) — none can ever show frozen=true. The value is correctly written to the store and schema (SCHEMA in src/store.js:12 includes frozenAt, and the raw row round-trips it; AccountCache invalidates correctly on the write), so this is purely a serializer omission, not a storage bug.
SITES: [{"file": "src/serialize.js", "line": 9, "title": "publicAccount never serializes frozen state"}, {"file": "src/serialize.js", "line": 9, "title": "publicAccount never exposes frozen state"}]
ROOTCAUSE: publicAccount() in src/serialize.js was never updated to expose frozen/frozenAt (unlike closedAt -> closed), so every API response for an account — including the freeze/unfreeze responses themselves and GET /accounts/:id — is indistinguishable between a frozen and an unfrozen account.

title: Rollback silently unfreezes accounts
loc: src/store.js : 95 | category: migrations-and-rollout
foundBy: ['migrations-and-rollout'] | verifiedBy: ['refute:p3.1', 'refute:p3.2', 'refute:p3.3']
SUMMARY: store.update()'s write path filters every row through pick(SCHEMA[collection], ...), so if the server is ever rolled back to the pre-PR commit (whose accounts SCHEMA has no frozenAt) while the data file already has a frozen account, the next unrelated write to that row silently strips frozenAt from the record instead of leaving it intact, defeating the freeze with no audit trail.
FAILURE: Confirmed by direct repro against this worktree's src/store.js: insert a row with frozenAt set, then simulate the base commit's accounts SCHEMA (no 'frozenAt') and call store.update('accounts', id, { interestRateBps: 150 }) -- an edit that never touches frozenAt. The returned/stored row comes back with the frozenAt key gone entirely ('frozenAt' in updated -> false), not merely unset. Every call site treats a frozen account by `if (account.frozenAt)`, so a missing key reads identically to 'never frozen': transfers.js's `if (from.frozenAt || to.frozenAt) throw ...` guard no longer fires, and the account that was frozen because a member's card was lost is silently transferable again -- with no admin action, no account.unfreeze audit entry, and the card processor never told it's unfrozen. Worse, this is not just an edge case: src/interest.js's accrueInterest() (the daily scheduled job, scripts/run-jobs.mjs interest) iterates every account with `if (account.closedAt) continue` -- it does NOT skip frozen accounts -- and calls store.update('accounts', account.id, {...}) on every account carrying a balance and rate. So after any rollback to the pre-PR commit, the very first scheduled interest run silently and systematically unfreezes every frozen, interest-bearing account in one pass, recorded only as an ordinary 'interest' audit entry that gives no hint the freeze was lost.
SITES: [{"file": "src/store.js", "line": 95, "title": "Rollback silently unfreezes accounts"}]
ROOTCAUSE: store.update()'s write path filters every row through pick(SCHEMA[collection], ...), so rolling the server back to the pre-PR code (whose accounts SCHEMA lacks frozenAt) causes the next unrelated update on a frozen account to silently strip frozenAt, un-freezing it with no audit trail.

findings.short_summary: Freeze webhook fires before ownership check
findings.summary: The POST /accounts/:id/freeze route sends the account.freeze-requested webhook to the card processor before freezeAccount() has checked that the caller owns the account (or that it isn't already frozen), so any signed-in user can trigger that third-party notification for an account they don't own.
findings.failure_scenario: POST /accounts/:id/freeze lets any signed-in user (not just the account's owner) trigger a real account.freeze-requested webhook delivery to the external card processor for an account they don't own, naming the real owner's accountId and the attacker's own id as requestedBy — because notify() at server.js:115 fires synchronously (unawaited) before freezeAccount() at server.js:116 performs the ownership check (404) or the already-frozen check (409) that would otherwise have blocked the request. Verified directly: a non-owner's freeze call returned 404 to the caller while the mocked webhook transport had already recorded one account.freeze-requested delivery for the target account. The same ordering also double-fires the webhook when an already-frozen account is frozen again. Violates docs/security.md's 'Authorisation first' rule and departs from the save-then-notify ordering every other mutating route in the file uses. The PR's own new test (test/server.test.js:136-154) never passes a `webhook` option to serve(), so createNotifier returns the no-op notifier and the test cannot observe the premature firing.

findings.summary: publicAccount(), the single function every account-returning route serializes through, has no field for frozenAt (unlike closedAt, which it already exposes as `closed`), so a frozen account's API representation is byte-for-byte identical to an unfrozen one.
findings.failure_scenario: A member calls POST /accounts/:id/freeze after losing a card. The handler returns HTTP 200 with body {id, label, currency, balanceCents, closed:false, createdAt} — no frozen indicator at all, identical to the pre-freeze body (verified live: the freeze response, a subsequent GET /accounts/:id, and GET /accounts are all identical to the unfrozen state, even though the raw store row shows frozenAt correctly set). The caller/UI that just froze the account cannot confirm the freeze took effect, and the only way any API consumer can discover an account is frozen is to attempt a transfer and receive the new 409. The same gap applies to the admin's unfreeze response and to every other account-returning route. The value is written to the store and schema correctly, so this is purely a serializer omission.

findings.summary: store.update()'s write path filters every row through pick(SCHEMA[collection], ...), so a rollback to the pre-PR commit (whose accounts SCHEMA has no frozenAt) causes the next unrelated write to a frozen row to silently strip frozenAt, defeating the freeze with no audit trail.
findings.failure_scenario: Confirmed by direct repro: insert a row with frozenAt set, simulate the base commit's accounts SCHEMA (no 'frozenAt'), then call store.update('accounts', id, { interestRateBps: 150 }) — an edit that never touches frozenAt. The stored row comes back with the frozenAt key gone entirely, not merely unset. Every call site tests `if (account.frozenAt)`, so a missing key reads identically to 'never frozen': transfers.js's guard stops firing and the account frozen over a lost card is silently transferable again, with no admin action, no unfreeze audit entry, and the card processor never told. Not just an edge case: accrueInterest() in src/interest.js (the daily scheduled job) skips only closedAt accounts and calls store.update() on every account with a balance and rate, so after a rollback the first scheduled interest run systematically unfreezes every frozen interest-bearing account in one pass, logged only as an ordinary 'interest' audit entry.

**Status: complete.** 3 root causes, all introduced by this PR — nothing pre-existing, nothing refuted, nothing left unverified. Baseline `npm run check && npm test` passed clean on the head commit, so none of this is a pre-broken tree.

Severities, in the order reported: **critical** (`src/server.js:115`, upheld 3/3 after a skeptic corrected its scope), **high** (`src/serialize.js:9`, upheld 3/3), **high / PLAUSIBLE** (`src/store.js:95`, a panel split 2–1 — the mechanism was reproduced, but one skeptic doubted the rollback premise, so treat it as not fully nailed down).

The critical finding was found independently by four of the seven angles, and its `sites` all point at the same spot in the freeze handler — one defect, not four.

**Budget:** used 19 of 20 — 1 scout, 7 finders, 1 triage, 9 skeptics (three-lens panels on all three root causes, since every one was critical or high), 1 critic. No retries, no agents lost, and the same-site check never ran because triage left no two groups at one location (`merged: 0`).

**Angles:** the six fixed ones all ran, sharpened at this diff — authz-and-attribution, data-integrity, silent-drops, tests-that-dont-test, migrations-and-rollout, correctness — plus one the scout added, *frozen-account invariant scope across subsystems*. The scout dropped two with reasons: **security** (no injection, secret, SSRF or CORS surface here; the one security-shaped issue was already authz's) and **boundary-contract** (the real mismatches it traced were the serializer and schema-whitelist sites already assigned elsewhere). The ceiling cut nothing.

**Verification:** 3 of 3 upheld, 0 refuted, 1 upheld only after correction, 0 downgraded. Nothing was dismissed for doubt alone.

### Not verified — for you to check by hand

`unverified` is empty, but the critic named three things **no angle looked at**. These have not survived refutation, though the critic reports reproducing each:

1. **`accrueInterest` in `src/interest.js` never skips frozen accounts** — it skips only `closedAt`. Seeding a frozen account and running the job grew its balance (100000 → 100013). A frozen account's balance keeps moving every day it sits frozen. Missed because every angle traced callers out from the new functions, and `scripts/run-jobs.mjs` is a separate entry point that never calls freeze.
2. **`closeAccount` never checks `frozenAt`** — freeze an account as owner (200), then `POST /accounts/:id/close` with the same owner token succeeds. The owner can unilaterally terminate a frozen account, the one lifecycle step the PR says only an admin controls.
3. **`freezeAccount` itself never checks `closedAt`** — unlike every sibling in `accounts.js`. Closing an account then freezing it returns 200 and fires the urgent webhook for an account that can no longer move money.

Worktrees for `wf_c1ee502c-958` all removed; your checkout is untouched (`main` @ `7fc1c3c`, clean). Result JSON written to `calibration/results/0.4.0/pr-19.json`. Nothing posted — `--no-post`.
